# Rollout Plan: Migrating 40,000 Users from Legacy Billing to New Billing System

## Overview

Both billing systems will run in parallel (dual-write / shadow mode where applicable) for the duration of the migration. Users are moved in batches; the legacy system remains live and authoritative for unmigrated users throughout. No decommissioning of the old system occurs until a dedicated post-migration phase, separate from the final migration batch.

---

## Phase 1: Pilot (2% of users — ~800 users)

**Entry criterion:** New billing system has passed end-to-end integration testing in staging, including invoice generation, payment capture, refunds, tax calculation, and reconciliation against legacy ledger formats; rollback procedure has been tested and confirmed to restore a migrated user to legacy billing with no data loss.

**Scope:** Internal employee accounts and volunteer opt-in customers only (low-revenue-risk, high-tolerance users). Manual monitoring, daily reconciliation of billing outputs between old and new systems for this cohort.

**Duration:** Minimum 2 weeks or 1 full billing cycle, whichever is longer, to observe at least one complete invoice/renewal cycle per user.

---

## Phase 2: Expansion (25% of users — ~10,000 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 1 completes with zero critical billing discrepancies (defined as any discrepancy affecting charge amount or payment method), less than 0.5% of Phase 1 users requiring manual billing correction, and support ticket volume for migrated users within 1.5x of baseline legacy support volume.

**Scope:** Randomized cross-section of the user base, stratified by plan type, geography, and payment method (credit card, ACH, invoice/PO) to surface edge cases across billing configurations. Automated reconciliation jobs replace manual daily checks, running hourly.

**Duration:** Minimum 3 weeks, covering at least one renewal cycle for annual and monthly plans represented in the cohort.

---

## Phase 3: General Availability (73% of users — remaining ~29,200 users)

**Entry criterion:** Phase 2 completes with zero critical (charge/payment-affecting) discrepancies, manual correction rate below 0.3%, automated reconciliation match rate at or above 99.9% for two consecutive weeks, and on-call/support teams have signed off on runbooks for the full range of edge cases observed in Phases 1–2.

**Scope:** All remaining users, migrated in weekly sub-batches of no more than 15% of total user base per batch to preserve rollback capacity and support bandwidth. Legacy system remains fully operational and dual-write continues for at least 30 days after the last user is migrated, to allow for late-arriving disputes, chargebacks, and billing corrections.

**Note:** Decommissioning, disabling, or deleting the old billing system is explicitly out of scope for this phase and is deferred to a separate Phase 4 (Legacy Decommission), which does not begin until Phase 3's final batch has completed a full billing cycle with no unresolved critical issues.

---

## Halt Metric

If, at any point during Phase 1, 2, or 3, the **billing discrepancy rate** (charges that do not match expected amount, currency, or payment method between old and new system outputs during the dual-write reconciliation window) **exceeds 1.0% of migrated users in any rolling 24-hour window**, the rollout halts immediately: no further users are migrated into the current phase, and the incident is triaged before any batch resumes. A secondary halt trigger: failed-payment rate among migrated users exceeding 2x the pre-migration baseline failure rate for that user segment, sustained over 48 hours.

---

## Risks

RISK: New system miscalculates tax or currency conversion for a subset of international users | Run parallel invoice generation in shadow mode for all users before their batch migrates, and diff against legacy output prior to cutover | Billing Engineering Lead
RISK: Payment method tokens fail to migrate correctly, causing failed charges | Pre-validate token migration in a dry run against a payment gateway sandbox for every batch before live cutover, with automated token-validity checks | Payments Platform Team
RISK: Customer support is overwhelmed by billing confusion during dual-system operation | Stand up a dedicated migration support queue with escalation runbooks, staffed ahead of each phase based on prior phase ticket volume | Customer Support Manager
RISK: Reconciliation gaps between old and new systems go undetected, causing revenue leakage or duplicate charges | Automated hourly reconciliation jobs with alerting on any mismatch above threshold, reviewed daily by finance ops during active migration | Finance Operations Lead
RISK: Rollback of a migrated user back to legacy billing is untested at scale and fails under real load | Conduct a rollback game-day exercise with a batch-sized synthetic load before Phase 2 begins | Site Reliability Engineering Lead

PHASES: 3
